gaps.problem: This sentence introduces automated continuous-integration pipeline jargon and internal software test-suite tracking that never appear in published PRD papers.
gaps.change: Delete this sentence entirely.

gaps.quote: This paragraph was rewritten in round r17 after review ticket OI-131, and the earlier wording is kept in the project records.

gaps.change: Delete this sentence entirely.

gaps.quote: We then went back and reran the whole chain a second time, just to be safe, and nothing changed.
gaps.problem: The informal, conversational phrasing ("went back and reran", "just to be safe") reads like an informal lab notebook rather than the objective, professional register of PRD.
gaps.change: Remove this sentence or replace it with a formal statement confirming that re-executing the analysis pipeline yields identical results.

gaps.quote: The companion analysis note [14] gives the full validation record, the construction of the uncertainties, and the tests with their assumptions, and it is cited below by section.
gaps.problem: Published PRD papers are self-contained archival records and do not repeatedly cite an inaccessible internal collaboration note by section as a proxy for methodology and validation records.
gaps.change: Replace the reference to the internal note with a self-contained summary in the text or an accessible supplemental material document.

gaps.quote: The joint-test estimator keeps five iterations because 10, 15, or 20 iterations did not reduce its model dependence, measured as the largest residual proxy over the truth changes used in its development.
gaps.problem: Narrating the chronological sequence of discarded test configurations and development history departs from the concise, outcome-oriented reporting of PRD papers (e.g., Ref. [2], Sec. V B: "As a result of these studies, unfolding is performed with 10 iterations for this analysis.").
gaps.change: State directly that five iterations were chosen because additional iterations yielded no significant reduction in model dependence.

gaps.quote: The two-observable central value uses LightGBM at seed 42 [23] with negative-weight background subtraction and a refinement of 400 trees and 31 leaves.
gaps.problem: Citing an arbitrary software execution seed ("seed 42") elevates code-level scripting details into methodological specifications, which PRD papers omit (e.g., Ref. [1], Sec. IV).
gaps.change: Remove the specific random seed number and describe the gradient-boosting setup purely in terms of its algorithmic architecture and hyperparameters.

gaps.quote: The joint-test estimator is a deterministic LightGBM (fixed seeds, reproducible training), and the refinement classifier of the two-observable estimator is seeded at the estimator seed plus three.
gaps.problem: Explaining that a component is "seeded at the estimator seed plus three" reports software implementation bookkeeping rather than physical or statistical methodology.
gaps.change: Delete the reference to relative seed arithmetic and state simply that fixed random seeds were used to ensure reproducible classifier training.

gaps.quote: Interval coverage has not been validated.
gaps.problem: This clipped, isolated declaration reads like an internal review checklist bullet or auditor caveat rather than the continuous, integrated prose of a PRD article.
gaps.change: Expand this note into a complete, professional explanation describing the specific coverage checks performed and the statistical boundaries of the evaluation.

gaps.quote: Our precision target is a 10 % median half-width for the total 68% interval.
gaps.problem: Framing the analysis around an internal project management requirement or milestone target departs from the standard PRD register of reporting observed measurement uncertainties.
gaps.change: Rephrase to report the achieved precision across the phase space directly without reference to internal project design targets.

gaps.quote: The three- and four-observable central values and the sixteen-cell five-observable result (Sec. V) use the joint-test estimator, a deterministic LightGBM with the same background treatment and refinement capacity.
gaps.problem: The term "joint-test estimator" is an unedited project-internal moniker rather than a standard, descriptive scientific label (contrast with "UniFold, MultiFold, and OmniFold" in Ref. [1], Sec. IV).
gaps.change: Replace the project-internal moniker with a descriptive designation such as "multidimensional boosted-decision-tree estimator."

gaps.quote: The variants used in development, and the results that rest on them, are described in Ref. [14], Sec. 3.2.
gaps.problem: Chronicling intermediate development variants and directing readers to an internal technical note for them clutters the article with obsolete development history.
gaps.change: Remove the reference to discarded development variants and focus the narrative strictly on the estimator configuration used in the final measurement.

gaps.quote: Those uncertainties come from an earlier purity-subtracted five-observable covariance that fails its specified acceptance criteria (Ref. [14], Sec. 9.6).

gaps.problem: The loosely parallel list and vague reference to “the coverage failure” turn the diagnostic’s scope into a defensive catalogue.
gaps.change: State precisely which conclusion the diagnostic supports and briefly identify the questions it does not assess.

gaps.quote: Because the block is built from the observed differences among the periods, its size is not validated and its own consistency check cannot fail.
gaps.problem: “Its own consistency check cannot fail” is conversational shorthand that leaves the relationship between construction and validation unclear.
gaps.change: Explain directly that a check using the same period differences does not independently validate the uncertainty estimate.

gaps.quote: This makes the two-dimensional result reusable, the higher-dimensional central values usable for qualitative comparison, and the sixteen-cell result usable for the comparison that follows.
gaps.problem: Repeated forms of “usable” produce an administrative classification of outputs rather than a direct statement of their interpretation.
gaps.change: State concisely which results support quantitative comparisons and which support qualitative comparisons.

gaps.quote: We make no coverage claim on independent simulated samples or simultaneously over all reported bins and projections.
gaps.problem: This repeats the adjacent statement that coverage has not been tested and adopts a disclaimer-like formulation.
gaps.change: Consolidate it with the preceding coverage statement, specifying the untested pointwise and simultaneous coverage in one sentence.

gaps.quote: The limitations of these results are stated with the results they qualify, in Secs. III–V, and those of the calibrated tests in the companion note.
gaps.problem: The limitations section opens with an inventory of where qualifications have been recorded rather than their substantive implications.
gaps.change: Remove the inventory and introduce the principal limitations directly.
